## DESCRIPTION

Inherits the fixed-return local query API of :obj:`LibTmux::Selection <LibTmux::Selection>`. Members must be defined :obj:`LibTmux::Client <LibTmux::Client>` handles from one server generation. Empty instances still validate against the client schema. Native array edits are possible; query methods validate membership and never perform tmux I/O.
doc.summary: Native array selection of captured client entities
`count($criteria?)` returns an integer. Empty input returns zero. Validate all members before evaluating the optional criterion; count every matching occurrence, including duplicates.
`exists($criteria?)` returns a native Boolean. Empty input returns false. After validating the entire membership, stop at the first matching entity. A reference itself remains true even when empty.
`first($criteria?)` returns the first matching entity or undef. Input order determines first; after membership validation, later field reads may be skipped.

`grep($callback)` returns a new same-class selection. Invoke the callback in scalar context with exactly one entity argument and a localized `$_`. Both bindings hold copies of the reference: assignment cannot replace a source slot. Restore `$_` and propagate the original thrown value even on failure. Predicates must not edit the traversed sequence.

Return a fresh local cursor with a copy of current membership. Its `next` returns an entity or undef only at exhaustion. Later native array edits do not alter this traversal; the selection remains replayable.

doc.body: Members may come from separate captures of the same server generation; each retains its own observation. Mixing servers or daemon generations throws :obj:`"InvalidSelection" in LibTmux::X <LibTmux::X::InvalidSelection>`. Combining captures does not reconcile their times.
doc.summary: `new(@entities)` creates a concrete blessed array reference and validates every member. Construct an entity-specific selection such as :obj:`LibTmux::PaneSelection <LibTmux::PaneSelection>`; an empty instance retains that schema.

`one($criteria?)` returns one entity. Zero throws :obj:`NoMatch <LibTmux::X::NoMatch>`; a second occurrence throws :obj:`MultipleMatches <LibTmux::X::MultipleMatches>`, reporting at least two and their IDs. Two occurrences of one identity are still ambiguous.
`one_or_undef($criteria?)` returns an entity or undef for absence. A second matching occurrence still throws :obj:`MultipleMatches <LibTmux::X::MultipleMatches>`.

Return a fresh, unblessed array reference containing the same entity references. Editing its membership cannot corrupt graph adjacency or this selection. Captured entity values remain read-only through public readers.

`where($criteria_or_filter)` eagerly returns a new selection of the same concrete class in scalar, list, or void context. Complete validation precedes evaluation, including on empty input. See :obj:`"new" in LibTmux::Filter <LibTmux::Filter::new>`. Order and duplicate occurrences are preserved.

Return a fresh literal argument array for a caller-owned interactive terminal without I/O. The session target is a stable ID string; obtain it through :obj:`"id" in LibTmux::Session <LibTmux::Session::id>`. The caller owns terminal/process setup and exit observation; the bounded capture transport does not allocate a TTY.     my $argv = $server->attach_argv(session => '$1');

Perform ordered independent literal requests and return a fresh array reference of {result, error} records in input order. Each result is :obj:`LibTmux::CommandResult <LibTmux::CommandResult>` or undef; each dispatch error is the original typed :obj:`LibTmux::X <LibTmux::X>` or undef. Nonzero command exits stay raw results. An empty input returns an empty array without command I/O. Requests are attempted in order, without rollback or tmux command-list attribution.


```perl
    my $results = $server->batch([['display-message', '-p', '#{version}']]);
```

## DESCRIPTION

Inherits the fixed-return local query API of :obj:`LibTmux::Selection <LibTmux::Selection>`. Members must be defined :obj:`LibTmux::Session <LibTmux::Session>` handles from one server generation. Empty instances still validate against the session schema. Native array edits are possible; query methods validate membership and never perform tmux I/O.
doc.summary: Native array selection of captured session entities
`count($criteria?)` returns an integer. Empty input returns zero. Validate all members before evaluating the optional criterion; count every matching occurrence, including duplicates.
`exists($criteria?)` returns a native Boolean. Empty input returns false. After validating the entire membership, stop at the first matching entity. A reference itself remains true even when empty.
`first($criteria?)` returns the first matching entity or undef. Input order determines first; after membership validation, later field reads may be skipped.

`grep($callback)` returns a new same-class selection. Invoke the callback in scalar context with exactly one entity argument and a localized `$_`. Both bindings hold copies of the reference: assignment cannot replace a source slot. Restore `$_` and propagate the original thrown value even on failure. Predicates must not edit the traversed sequence.

Return a fresh local cursor with a copy of current membership. Its `next` returns an entity or undef only at exhaustion. Later native array edits do not alter this traversal; the selection remains replayable.

doc.body: Members may come from separate captures of the same server generation; each retains its own observation. Mixing servers or daemon generations throws :obj:`"InvalidSelection" in LibTmux::X <LibTmux::X::InvalidSelection>`. Combining captures does not reconcile their times.
doc.summary: `new(@entities)` creates a concrete blessed array reference and validates every member. Construct an entity-specific selection such as :obj:`LibTmux::PaneSelection <LibTmux::PaneSelection>`; an empty instance retains that schema.

`one($criteria?)` returns one entity. Zero throws :obj:`NoMatch <LibTmux::X::NoMatch>`; a second occurrence throws :obj:`MultipleMatches <LibTmux::X::MultipleMatches>`, reporting at least two and their IDs. Two occurrences of one identity are still ambiguous.
`one_or_undef($criteria?)` returns an entity or undef for absence. A second matching occurrence still throws :obj:`MultipleMatches <LibTmux::X::MultipleMatches>`.

Return a fresh, unblessed array reference containing the same entity references. Editing its membership cannot corrupt graph adjacency or this selection. Captured entity values remain read-only through public readers.

`where($criteria_or_filter)` eagerly returns a new selection of the same concrete class in scalar, list, or void context. Complete validation precedes evaluation, including on empty input. See :obj:`"new" in LibTmux::Filter <LibTmux::Filter::new>`. Order and duplicate occurrences are preserved.

## EXECUTION

All methods in this module operate on local captured data and perform no tmux I/O. Ordering is deterministic; public query methods do not mutate membership. Typed validation/evaluation errors propagate. See :obj:`"snapshot" in LibTmux::Server <LibTmux::Server::snapshot>` for explicit acquisition and :obj:`LibTmux::X <LibTmux::X>` for machine-readable failures.

Return a fresh :obj:`LibTmux::ClientSelection <LibTmux::ClientSelection>` in captured order. A loaded empty client set is valid.
Return the capture completeness Boolean. The strict live acquisition path fails on incomplete topology; it does not synthesize empty relations.

`from_records(server_id => ..., generation => ..., sessions => [...], windows => [...], window_links => [...], panes => [...], clients => [...])` constructs a detached graph. Scalar records and relation IDs are copied. Omitted fields/collections remain unloaded; null is explicit. Invalid identities or inconsistent complete topology throw typed acquisition errors.
Return the captured daemon generation. :obj:`LibTmux::Server <LibTmux::Server>` checks it before mutations through captured handles; retained snapshots never silently refresh.
Return a fresh metadata hash with capture start/end, daemon version, and PID where acquired. Several commands observe an interval; the snapshot is not an atomic tmux transaction.
`pane_by_id('%3')` returns a :obj:`LibTmux::Pane <LibTmux::Pane>` or undef. The returned handle retains the captured graph after this wrapper goes out of scope.
Return a fresh :obj:`LibTmux::PaneSelection <LibTmux::PaneSelection>` containing each physical pane identity once. Membership edits cannot change the graph store.
Return the captured server scope. Entity IDs are meaningful only within this scope and :obj:`"generation" <LibTmux::Snapshot::generation>`.
`session_by_id('$1')` returns a :obj:`LibTmux::Session <LibTmux::Session>` or undef. Single quotes preserve the dollar-prefixed ID instead of interpolating a regex capture.
Return a fresh :obj:`LibTmux::SessionSelection <LibTmux::SessionSelection>` in captured order. Empty loaded collections yield empty selections; unloaded collections throw.
